newsitem.title: GHANA: Meningitis kills over 400 people in north Ghana.
newsitem.headline: Meningitis kills over 400 people in north Ghana.

text.p: An outbreak of meningitis in northern Ghana has killed more than 400 people, mainly children, since the beginning of the year, health ministry figures showed.
Ghana is on the edge of a belt of countries across Sub-Saharan Africa traditionally ravaged by the disease at this time of year.
The ministry figures reported 3,757 cases in Upper-East, Upper-West and Northern Region, of which 411 had proved fatal.
A ministry official said two planes with medical staff and supplies had left for the northern town of Tamale on Friday.
The Dutch branch of Medecins Sans Frontieres said it had a plane with vaccines and medical staff in Accra waiting for permission to fly north.
Meningitis is an inflammation of the brain and spinal cord which torments arid regions of Africa during the dry season. Babies and young children are the main victims.
The World Health Organisation described 1996 as the worst year on record for meningitis in Africa, with around 150,000 reported cases and 16,000 deaths.
It said on March 7, that this year's epidemic had killed 1,506 people -- 724 of them in Burkina Faso. Benin, Gambia, Togo, Niger and Mali were among other nations hit this year.

Chad and Nigeria are among other countries in the region's meningitis belt, which extends from Senegal to Ethiopia. Health workers say the belt is moving south, in the absence of monitoring and vaccination campaigns.
